title: candidate-clarity-timeline-and-open-asks
notes:
Candidate: Jordan Reyes (sourced via referrals)
Role: Senior Runtime Engineer (serving/runtime)
Interview loop: take-home -> pairing session -> system-design -> final panel

Quick gut (first pass):
- Thoughtful answers on KV caching and tradeoffs, but used some shorthand that masked gaps (e.g., assumed availability of bespoke ops).
- Very product-aware — brought examples of reducing p99 by changing batching policy and showed impact numbers.
- Communication was conversational but occasionally jumped to low-level impl before clarifying requirements.

Timeline & context:
- 2024-09-24: phone screen (30m) with TA — clears baseline.
- 2024-10-01: take-home (4 hours) returned; code readable, test coverage minimal.
- 2024-10-05: pairing (90m) with me + Samir — implemented a prototype of a prefix cache eviction policy.
- 2024-10-11: system-design (60m) with Evelyn — sketched autoscaling + routing policy for mixed-latency workloads.

Strengths observed:
- Practical tradeoff framing: latency vs cost vs complexity. Gave concrete numbers from past infra work.
- Familiarity with GPU memory constraints and KV cache heuristics.
- Empathy for product owners; able to translate infra tradeoffs into user-facing metrics.

Risks / open questions:
- Implementation detail hygiene: some variable naming and test assumptions in take-home would make long-lived code brittle (needs stronger review habits).
- Gap in formal benchmarking methodology; relied on anecdotal runs, no reproducible harness shown.
- Limited experience with multi-tenant routing policies at scale — did not discuss how to safely roll out new routing rules across tenants.

Concrete evidence snippets (quotes):
- "We usually tune the batcher based on tail latency percentiles rather than average because p99 is the thing that kills SLAs." (positive)
- "I hacked the eviction to be LRU-ish but we just check tokens per request and evict the biggest ones first" (signals pragmatic, but patchy).

Candidate questions that remain (to resolve before hire):
- Can they produce a reproducible microbenchmark for batching/eviction performance within 2 weeks?
- How do they approach automated rollout safety for routing policy changes (can they outline a canary + rollback plan)?
- Will they adopt our testing guardrails (benchmarks-as-tests + perf regression CI)?

Suggested follow-ups / mitigations if moving forward:
- Mini take-home 2: reproducible benchmark + perf report (4–6 hours). Focus: batcher with synthetic traffic and measured p50/p95/p99.
- Pair with SRE/observability (1 session) to assess instrumentation mindset and metrics selection.
- Add a probation objective around "benchmarks as tests" to ensure reproducibility.

Scorecard (subjective, 1–5):
- Technical (algorithms & systems): 4/5
- Implementation hygiene (tests/docs): 2.5/5
- Design for scale (multi-tenant routing): 3/5
- Communication & stakeholder sync: 4/5

Hiring recommendation (tentative):
- Move to "exercise and SRE pair" stage rather than immediate hire. Strong on product tradeoffs and runtime intuition; wants to see disciplined benchmarking and cleaner long-term code habits.

Notes for debrief with panel:
- Ask Jordan to walk through a concrete rollback timeline for a routing policy change.
- Bring up the take-home tests specifically: point to two small file lines that are brittle and ask how they'd refactor.
- Probe their experience with perf regression CI — do they have an example where a pipeline caught a regression?

Misc scratch:
- Can Samir share the perf harness template we use? Attach link in the follow-up email.
- If we proceed to offer, tie compensation expectations to 2-week deliverable (benchmark + doc).
next_steps: Send mini take-home (benchmark) within 2 business days; schedule 1-hour SRE pairing next week; prepare panel notes highlighting rollback question.
